title: Optimal approximation ratio for shortest common superstring
formal: Determine \(\rho _{\mathrm{SCS}}=\inf\){\(r\ge 1: a\) uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm returns a feasible solution of objective value at most \(r\cdot\)OPT on every shortest common superstring instance}, in the input and output model below.
definitions: Symbols are integers from \(\{1,\ldots ,\sigma\}\), encoded in binary; \(\sigma\) and all strings are input. Running time is measured on a deterministic Turing machine in the total bit length of this explicit representation. String length counts symbols. Repeated and empty input strings are allowed. For an empty collection, OPT is zero. The output is an explicit string over the input alphabet, and containment means ordinary forward contiguous occurrence without reversal, reverse complementation or cyclic wraparound. All preprocessing is charged. For each fixed ratio r in the defining set, one finite deterministic algorithm and one time polynomial must work on every instance; both may depend on r. The infimum is over these globally uniform guarantees and need not be attained. There is no per-input-size choice of algorithm, advice or free optimization oracle.

context_blocks.text: The target is the infimum polynomial-time approximation ratio. The factor-two algorithmic question discussed in the saved history selects one threshold in this larger numerical target.
Shortest common superstring formalizes assembly of overlapping sequences. The unresolved factor two is an approximation barrier for the problem itself, regardless of the algorithm used.

An August 2026 preprint gives a \(7/3\) approximation. A separate September preprint claims a counterexample to the factor-two guarantee for maximum-overlap greedy. Even if that claim is correct, it concerns a particular algorithm and does not answer the general existence question here.

why: A long-standing approximation threshold for a basic string-assembly problem with direct algorithmic genomics and compression motivation.
answer_criterion: Supply a specified real number a and prove in Lean that |\(a- \rho _{\mathrm{SCS}}|\le 1/100\). The proof must certify both a lower and an upper bound for the unrestricted quantity in this card. Equivalently, certified bounds \(\ell\)\(\le u\) of width at most \(1/50\) qualify by taking \(a=(\ell +u)/2\). An exact value with proof of equality also qualifies. An unevaluated copy of the defining extremum, a one-sided improvement, or a numerical estimate without a proved error bound does not meet this criterion. The \(1/100\) tolerance is benchmark acceptance; it does not prove an associated exact threshold conjecture. Any hardness assumption must be stated explicitly; a conditional lower bound establishes only its conditional conclusion.

progress.text: The August 2026 report claims a \(7/3\) general approximation and a factor-three upper bound for maximum-overlap greedy.
A 1 September 2026 preprint claims a \(9/4\) lower bound for greedy. This report records the claim without certifying its proof; it does not refute general 2-approximation.

sentences: A common superstring contains every supplied string as a contiguous substring.
The objective is to minimize its length over the input alphabet.
The target is the infimum approximation ratio of uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithms.
The algorithm must return a feasible string, with input and output costs measured in the stated bit model.
The Lean benchmark accepts a certified value of this ratio within absolute error 0.01.
